title: Databricks closes $5B at $190B, past $7B revenue run-rate
subtitle: Coatue-led round marks the company's second raise of 2026, with capital going to Lakebase, the Genie coworker, and Unity AI Gateway.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Databricks announced on August 13 that it has closed a $5 billion strategic growth round led by Coatue Management, with Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price and Sixth Street Growth participating. The round values the company at $190 billion — up from $134 billion in February and $62 billion in January 2025 — and Databricks said its revenue run-rate has passed $7 billion, with 80% year-over-year growth in Q2.

The stated use of proceeds points at three products, not one. Lakebase is Databricks' serverless Postgres purpose-built for AI agents, which need transactional read-write against fresh data rather than the analytical scans Databricks was originally designed for. Genie is the AI coworker layer that sits on top of the lakehouse. Unity AI Gateway is the piece that meters, routes and governs traffic across multiple model providers — the same problem Anthropic's own AI Gateway and every enterprise MLOps vendor is trying to own. The three together are Databricks' bid to be the platform companies deploy agents on, not just the platform they analyze data on.

The valuation puts Databricks in the same weight class as Anthropic's most recent round and pushes it well past every other enterprise-data vendor. It is also a datapoint on where the private AI capital is going: not to another foundation-model lab, but to the layer between the labs and the customer. The two largest deals of the last quarter have both been infrastructure — Databricks now, and NVIDIA's $500 billion Wall Street financing alliance from two days ago. The model race is priced; the deployment race isn't.

Takeaway for learners: 'AI company' is now three different jobs. There are labs (train the model), there are agent platforms (turn the model into a system that acts), and there are gateways (govern which model gets called and what it costs). Understanding which layer a product sits at is more useful than knowing which model it uses. Databricks used to be a data company; today's raise is priced as if it is now an agent company that happens to own the data plane too.
